mainTopic: Judging alone, and what official permission (רשות) to judge does, where it works, and what it contained
overview: The ברייתא says a recognized expert may judge alone, and רב נחמן and רבי חייא each say that 'someone like me' may judge money cases alone. The גמרא asks whether 'like me' also requires official permission (רשות). A story about מר זוטרא and רב יוסף shows that a ruling counts even without permission. רב and שמואל then teach what permission does add: a judge who has permission from the ריש גלותא is exempt from paying if he makes a mistake. Permission works in its own land, and permission from בבל also works in ארץ ישראל, because the ריש גלותא is a 'scepter' and the נשיא only a 'staff'. A story about רבה בר חנה proves that permission from ארץ ישראל does not work in בבל, though it does work in the border towns. The גמרא then describes the permission רבי gave רבה בר חנה and רב, and asks why רבי חייא called one 'my brother's son' and the other 'my sister's son'. A second answer to that question begins at the end of the עמוד and continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: An expert may judge alone
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a judge who is recognized as an expert by the public may judge even by himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he was an expert recognized by the public, he may judge even alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing to quote the ברייתא from earlier on the דף. Normally a court needs three judges, but here it makes an exception for a recognized expert.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually monetary cases need a בית דין of three. This line adds an exception: a מומחה לרבים can sit as a single judge. The rest of this passage builds on this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: An expert recognized by the public

phrases.english: But if he was an expert for the public,
he may judge even alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם הָיָה מוּמְחֶה לְרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from earlier on the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A judge recognized by the public as an expert may judge monetary cases alone.

steps.title: רב נחמן and רבי חייא say 'someone like me' may judge alone
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן and רבי חייא each say that someone like them may judge monetary cases alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Someone like me may judge monetary cases alone. And רבי חייא said the same: Someone like me may judge monetary cases alone.
steps.whatsHappening: Two great אמוראים apply the ברייתא's rule to themselves. They say a person of their level may judge money cases by himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spoke generally about a מומחה. These two rabbis give a real example, themselves. But the phrase 'like me' is unclear, and the next step asks exactly what it includes.

keyTerms.meaning: And similarly said, the same ruling from another rabbi

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן אֲנָא דָּן דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת בִּיחִידִי.
phrases.english: Someone like me may judge monetary cases alone.
And similarly Rabbi Chiya said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן אֲנָא דָּן דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת בִּיחִידִי.
phrases.english: Someone like me may judge monetary cases alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: כְּגוֹן אֲנָא דָּן דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת בִּיחִידִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a concrete example of the ברייתא's rule about an expert judging alone.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A judge of the stature of רב נחמן or רבי חייא may judge monetary cases alone.

steps.title: Does 'like me' include having official permission?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether 'like me' means a scholar who also has official permission, so that without permission the ruling is invalid. Or does a ruling count even without permission?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Does 'like me' mean like me, who has learned, can reason, and holds permission, so that one who does not hold permission, his ruling is not a ruling? Or perhaps, even though he does not hold permission, his ruling is a ruling?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about the words 'like me.' Do they also include having official רשות to judge?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן and רבי חייא were learned, skilled at reasoning, and also had official permission. If 'like me' requires all three, then an expert without permission cannot give a valid ruling alone. The other side says knowledge and skill are enough, and permission is not needed for the ruling to count.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them
I have learned (I know the traditions)
I can reason and work out new rulings
Official permission or authorization to judge

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
"Like me" — who have learned and can reason
and hold permission,
but one who does not hold permission,
his ruling is not a ruling?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא נָקֵיט רְשׁוּתָא –
phrases.english: Or perhaps: even though he does not hold permission,
his ruling is a ruling?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what exactly the phrase 'like me' from step 2 includes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is official permission needed for a single expert's ruling to be valid, or is expertise enough?

steps.title: The story of מר זוטרא's mistaken ruling
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא, son of רב נחמן, judged a case and made a mistake. רב יוסף told him: if the two sides accepted you as judge, you do not pay; if not, go pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: מר זוטרא, son of רב נחמן, judged a case and made a mistake. He came before רב יוסף. רב יוסף said to him: If they accepted you upon themselves, you do not pay. And if not, go pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story to try to answer the question. In the story, רב יוסף decides whether a judge who made a mistake has to pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's answer depends only on whether the two sides accepted מר זוטרא as their judge. He does not ask whether מר זוטרא had official permission. The גמרא will use this to answer the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, introducing a proof
They accepted you upon themselves as their judge

phrases.english: Come and hear:
That Mar Zutra, son of Rav Nachman,
judged a case and made a mistake.
He came before Rav Yosef.
He said to him: If they accepted you upon themselves,
phrases.notes: 'They' are the two sides in the case, who agreed to have him as their judge.

phrases.english: you do not pay.
And if not, go pay.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: דְּמָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן דָּן דִּינָא וּטְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story to try to answer the question in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a single judge's ruling is valid without official permission.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יוסף's ruling to מר זוטרא, which depended only on whether the sides accepted him, with no mention of permission.

steps.title: Without permission, the ruling still counts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא learns from the story that even a judge without permission gives a valid ruling, and confirms this conclusion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it: even when he does not hold permission, his ruling is a ruling. Indeed, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the lesson from the story and settles the question. A ruling counts even without official permission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר זוטרא is understood not to have had permission. Yet רב יוסף said that if the sides accepted him, he does not pay, meaning his ruling counts as a real judgment. So 'like me' did not require permission for the ruling to be valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; the second time, it confirms: yes, learn from it
His ruling is a valid ruling

steps.whatToRemember: A single expert judge's ruling is valid even if he never received official permission (רשות).
steps.confusionAlert: The two שמע מינה's are not the same. The first one suggests the lesson, and the second one confirms it as the conclusion.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: כִּי לָא נָקֵיט רְשׁוּתָא –
phrases.english: Learn from it: when he does not hold permission,
his ruling is a ruling.
Indeed, learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: כִּי לָא נָקֵיט רְשׁוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the story in step 4 and answers the question in step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Even without official permission, a single expert's ruling is a valid ruling.

steps.title: Get permission from the ריש גלותא to be protected from paying for mistakes
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל teach that a judge who wants to be exempt from paying if he makes a mistake should get permission from the ריש גלותא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Whoever wants to judge a case, and wants to be exempt if he makes a mistake, should take permission from the house of the ריש גלותא. And similarly שמואל said: He should take permission from the house of the ריש גלותא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching from רב and שמואל. It explains what permission is good for: it protects a judge from paying for a mistaken ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last step showed that a ruling counts even without permission. Here we learn what permission adds: protection from paying if the judge makes a mistake. To get that protection, the permission must come from the ריש גלותא.

keyTerms.meaning: To be exempt, free from paying
The Exilarch, the head of the Jewish community in בבל

steps.whatToRemember: Permission is not needed for a ruling to count, but it protects a judge from paying if he errs. In בבל it comes from the ריש גלותא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the practical value of רשות: it is about protecting the judge from paying, not about whether his ruling is valid.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: הַאי מַאן דְּבָעֵי לְמֵידַן דִּינָא,
phrases.english: Rav said: Whoever wants to judge a case,
and wants to be exempt if he makes a mistake,
should take permission from the house of the Exilarch.
And similarly Shmuel said:
He should take permission from the house of the Exilarch.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: הַאי מַאן דְּבָעֵי לְמֵידַן דִּינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing a ruling counts without permission, it teaches what permission does add: being exempt from paying for a mistake.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A judge who wants to be exempt from paying for a mistaken ruling must get permission from the ריש גלותא.

steps.title: Which permissions obviously work
steps.stepSummary: Permission from בבל works in בבל, and permission from ארץ ישראל works in ארץ ישראל. Permission from בבל also works in ארץ ישראל, because the ריש גלותא is a 'scepter' and the נשיא is only a 'staff'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that permission from here (בבל) works here, and permission from there (ארץ ישראל) works there. Permission from here also works there, because the leader here is a 'scepter' and the leader there is a 'staff'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists the easy cases of where a judge's permission works. This sets up the harder question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each leader's permission clearly works in his own land. Permission from the ריש גלותא also works in ארץ ישראל, because his power ('scepter') is greater than the נשיא's ('staff'). The one case not yet settled is permission from ארץ ישראל used in בבל.

keyTerms.meaning: Scepter: a ruler with real power
Staff: a lawgiver with less power

phrases.english: It is obvious: from here to here,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means בבל and 'there' means ארץ ישראל. He means permission given in one place and used in the other.

phrases.english: and from there to there, it works.
And from here to there it also works,
because here is a 'scepter' and there is a 'staff'.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא: מֵהָכָא לְהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 6's advice to get permission from the ריש גלותא and asks how far such permission reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Permission works in its own land, and permission from בבל also works in ארץ ישראל because the ריש גלותא has greater power.

steps.title: The verse behind 'scepter' and 'staff'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the פסוק: the 'scepter' is the ראשי גליות in בבל, who rule with power. The 'staff' is the descendants of הלל, who teach Torah in public.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'The scepter shall not depart from Judah' means the ראשי גליות in בבל, who rule the Jewish people with a rod. 'Nor the staff from between his feet' means the grandchildren of הלל, who teach Torah in public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up the 'scepter' and 'staff' line from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the פסוק as describing two kinds of leaders. The ריש גלותא has real ruling power, and the נשיא (from הלל's family) has teaching authority. This explains why permission from בבל counts as stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
The heads of the exile in בבל
הלל's descendants, the נשיאים in ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: As it is taught: 'The scepter shall not depart from Judah':
these are the heads of the exile in Babylonia,
who rule over Israel with a rod.
'Nor the staff from between his feet':
these are the grandchildren of Hillel,
who teach Torah in public.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the 'scepter' and 'staff' wording in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That the ריש גלותא has more power than the נשיא

steps.title: What about permission from ארץ ישראל used in בבל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether permission from ארץ ישראל works for judging in בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: From there to here, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the one case step 7 did not cover: permission from ארץ ישראל used in בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the נשיא's power is weaker, it is not clear that his permission works where the stronger ריש גלותא rules. The story in the next step answers this.

phrases.english: From there to here, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵהָתָם לְהָכָא מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the remaining case not covered by step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does permission from the נשיא in ארץ ישראל protect a judge in בבל?

steps.title: The story of רבה בר חנה's mistake
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר חנה judged a case and made a mistake. רבי חייא told him he must pay unless the two sides had accepted him, even though he had permission from ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבה בר חנה judged a case and made a mistake. He came before רבי חייא, who told him: if they accepted you, do not pay; if not, go pay. But רבה בר חנה had permission!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story to answer the question from step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר חנה had permission from ארץ ישראל but judged in בבל. Even so, רבי חייא said that only the two sides' acceptance could protect him. So his permission did not help him in בבל.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: brings a proof

phrases.english: Come and hear: for Rabba bar Hana
judged a case and made a mistake.
He came before Rabbi Hiyya.
He said to him: If they accepted you upon themselves,

phrases.aramaic: לָא תְּשַׁלֵּם, וְאִי לָא – זִיל שַׁלֵּים.
phrases.english: do not pay; and if not, go pay.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבָּה בַּר חָנָה רְשׁוּתָא הֲוָה נְקִיט!
phrases.english: But Rabba bar Hana had received permission!
phrases.notes: His permission came from ארץ ישראל, and he was judging in בבל. That's why this story fits the question.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: דְּרַבָּה בַּר חָנָה דָּן דִּינָא וּטְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story to answer step 9's question.
steps.raayaObject: That permission from ארץ ישראל does not protect a judge in בבל
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חייא's ruling to רבה בר חנה

steps.title: Permission from ארץ ישראל does not work in בבל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that permission from ארץ ישראל does not work in בבל, and confirms it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: from there to here, it does not work. Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws its conclusion from the story and agrees with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Permission goes from the stronger leader to the weaker leader's land, but not the other way. A judge in בבל needs permission from the ריש גלותא.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it: draws or confirms a conclusion

steps.whatToRemember: Permission from בבל works everywhere. Permission from ארץ ישראל does not protect a judge in בבל.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: מֵהָתָם לְהָכָא לָא מַהֲנֵי.
phrases.english: Learn from it: from there to here it does not work.
Yes, learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: מֵהָתָם לְהָכָא לָא מַהֲנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes from the story in step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Permission from ארץ ישראל is not effective in בבל.

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא's chain of permission
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the conclusion. רבה בר רב הונא told the house of the ריש גלותא that he did not need their permission. His permission came in a chain from his father, רב, רבי חייא, and רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does it really not work? But when רבה בר רב הונא argued with the house of the ריש גלותא, he said: I did not get permission from you. I got it from my father, he from רב, רב from רבי חייא, and רבי חייא from רבי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions its own conclusion with a story that seems to show permission from ארץ ישראל does work in בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chain goes back to רבי in ארץ ישראל. רבה בר רב הונא seemed to rely on it to judge in בבל without the ריש גלותא. That would mean permission from ארץ ישראל does work in בבל.

phrases.english: And does it not work?
But Rabba bar Rav Huna,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוָה מִינְּצֵי בַּהֲדֵי דְּבֵי רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא,
phrases.english: when he was quarreling with the house of the Exilarch,
said: I did not receive permission from you;
I received permission from my father, my master,
and my father, my master, from Rav,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב מֵרַבִּי חִיָּיא, וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא מֵרַבִּי!
phrases.english: and Rav from Rabbi Hiyya, and Rabbi Hiyya from Rabbi!
phrases.notes: 'רבי' here means רבי יהודה הנשיא in ארץ ישראל, so the chain starts there.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא מַהֲנֵי? וְהָא רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that permission from ארץ ישראל does not work in בבל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבה בר רב הונא relied on a chain of permission from רבי in ארץ ישראל to stand up to the ריש גלותא in בבל. That suggests it works.

steps.title: He was only pushing back with words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבה בר רב הונא was only arguing back with words. His claim had no real legal force.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was just standing up to them with mere words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the story does not prove anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר רב הונא's claim was something said in the heat of an argument, not a legal ruling. So the conclusion of step 11 stands: permission from ארץ ישראל does not work in בבל.

keyTerms.meaning: Stood up to, held them off

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge falls away. Permission from ארץ ישראל still does not protect a judge in בבל.

phrases.english: It was with mere words that he stood up to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמִילְּתָא דְעָלְמָא הוּא דְּאוֹקֵים לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Takes away the proof by saying the statement had no legal weight
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבה בר רב הונא's chain of permission really protected him in בבל.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was only talk to hold off the ריש גלותא's household, so the conclusion of step 11 stands.

steps.title: Why did רבה בר חנה take permission at all?
steps.stepSummary: If permission from ארץ ישראל does not work in בבל, why did רבה בר חנה take it with him?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the permission does not work in בבל, why did רבה בר חנה need to take it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own conclusion. If the permission is useless in בבל, why did רבה בר חנה bother getting it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 decided that רשות from ארץ ישראל has no power in בבל. Yet the story in step 10 shows רבה בר חנה carrying that רשות when he went to בבל. If it truly did nothing, taking it seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: Permission or authorization to rule or judge
Why do I need it? (asks what purpose something serves)

phrases.english: But since it is not effective,
phrases.notes: "It" is permission from ארץ ישראל, which we just learned does not work in בבל.

phrases.english: the permission that Rabba bar Chana took
why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דְּלָא מַהֲנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new difficulty against the conclusion of step 11, now that step 13 has answered the earlier challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that רשות from ארץ ישראל does not work in בבל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבה בר חנה took רשות with him to בבל. If it had no effect there, taking it would have been pointless.

steps.title: The permission works in the border towns
steps.stepSummary: The permission was useful for the towns on the border between the two regions.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was for the towns that stand on the borders.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the permission did have a use. It works in the towns sitting on the border.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from step 11 stays in place: inside בבל proper, permission from ארץ ישראל does not work. But border towns are not fully under בבל, so the permission still has force there. This explains why רבה בר חנה took it.

phrases.english: For the towns that stand on the borders.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָעֲיָירוֹת הָעוֹמְדִים עַל הַגְּבוּלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope: the permission has a use in a specific place
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the permission does not work in בבל, it seems to have no use at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: It does not work inside בבל proper, but it does work in the border towns.
steps.whatToRemember: Permission from ארץ ישראל does not work in בבל itself, but it does work in the border towns. That is why רבה בר חנה took it.

steps.title: What did the permission contain?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what this permission actually was.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was the permission?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: what exactly was in the permission? This short question sets up the story that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the permission has been mentioned only in general terms. Now the גמרא wants to know its details: what the person was allowed to do.

phrases.english: What was the permission?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי רְשׁוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from whether the permission works to what the permission included.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the permission given to רבה בר חנה actually contained

steps.title: The permission given to רבה בר חנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא asked רבי for permission for his nephew רבה בר חנה. רבי allowed him to rule, to judge, and to permit firstborn animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבה בר חנה was going down to בבל, רבי חייא said to רבי: 'My brother's son is going down to בבל. May he rule?' 'He may rule.' 'May he judge?' 'He may judge.' 'May he permit firstborn animals?' 'He may permit.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a story. רבי gave רבה בר חנה three powers: to rule on what is forbidden and permitted, to judge money cases, and to permit firstborn animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission was not one general license. It was a list of separate powers, each asked about and granted on its own. רבה בר חנה received all three.

keyTerms.meaning: Going down (traveling from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
He may rule on what is forbidden and permitted

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up יוֹרֵד and יוֹרֶה. יוֹרֵד means 'going down' to בבל. יוֹרֶה means 'may he rule' on what is forbidden and permitted.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוָה נָחֵית רַבָּה בַּר חָנָה לְבָבֶל,
phrases.english: When Rabba bar Chana was going down to Bavel,
Rabbi Chiyya said to Rebbi:
My brother's son is going down to Bavel.
"May he rule?" "He may rule!"
phrases.notes: This is about ruling on questions of what is forbidden and what is permitted.

phrases.english: "May he judge?" "He may judge!"
"May he permit firstborn animals?" "He may permit!"
phrases.notes: A firstborn animal with a lasting blemish may be eaten, but only after an expert permits it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲוָה נָחֵית רַבָּה בַּר חָנָה לְבָבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16 with a story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The permission was three separate powers (to rule, to judge, to permit firstborn animals), and all three were granted to רבה בר חנה.

steps.title: The permission given to רב
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא asked the same for רב. רבי allowed him to rule and to judge, but not to permit firstborn animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב was going down to בבל, רבי חייא said to רבי: 'My sister's son is going down to בבל. May he rule?' 'He may rule.' 'May he judge?' 'He may judge.' 'May he permit firstborn animals?' 'He may not permit.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a matching story about רב. He received the first two powers but was refused the third. The story also sets up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story shows that each power was granted separately, because רב got only two of the three. It also shows a change in wording: רבי חייא calls רב 'my sister's son' and not 'my brother's son.' The גמרא will now ask about these differences.

phrases.english: When Rav was going down to Bavel,
Rabbi Chiyya said to Rebbi:
My sister's son is going down to Bavel.
"May he rule?" "He may rule!"
"May he judge?" "He may judge!"
"May he permit firstborn animals?" "He may not permit!"

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲוָה נָחֵית רַב לְבָבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story to step 17, with one key difference in the outcome and one in the wording.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב was granted the powers to rule and to judge, but not the power to permit firstborn animals.

steps.title: Why the different family titles?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי חייא called רבה בר חנה 'my brother's son' but called רב 'my sister's son.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did he call this master 'my brother's son' and that master 'my sister's son'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the two stories use different wording and asks why. It starts with the family titles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two stories are almost word-for-word the same, so any difference stands out. The גמרא wants to know why רבי חייא described each nephew differently.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Why the difference?
Master (a respectful way to refer to a sage)

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא לְמָר דְּקָא קָרֵי ״בֶּן אָחִי״,
phrases.english: What is different about this master, that he calls him "my brother's son,"
phrases.notes: "This master" is רבה בר חנה, and "he" is רבי חייא.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי שְׁנָא לְמָר דְּקָא קָרֵי ״בֶּן אֲחוֹתִי״?
phrases.english: and what is different about that master, that he calls him "my sister's son"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא לְמָר דְּקָא קָרֵי בֶּן אָחִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up on a difference in wording between the two stories.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for the different family titles רבי חייא used for his two nephews

steps.title: Both nephews were brothers' sons
steps.stepSummary: You might say the titles simply reflect the facts. But a teaching says רב's father and רבה בר חנה's father were both brothers of רבי חייא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that is just how the family was, didn't the master say that איבו, חנה, שילא, מרתא, and רבי חייא were all children of אבא בר אחא כרסלא from כפרי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the easy answer that רב was simply a sister's son. A known teaching shows that רב's father was רבי חייא's brother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching lists איבו (רב's father) and חנה (רבה בר חנה's father) as siblings of רבי חייא. That makes רב a brother's son too, just like רבה בר חנה. So why call him 'my sister's son'?

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't the master say? (brings a teaching that contradicts)

phrases.english: And if you would say that this is how the facts were,
but didn't the master say:

phrases.aramaic: אַיְּבוּ וְחַנָּה וְשֵׁילָא וּמָרְתָא וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא
phrases.english: Aivu, and Chana, and Sheila, and Marta, and Rabbi Chiyya
phrases.notes: איבו is רב's father, and חנה is רבה בר חנה's father.

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלְּהוּ בְּנֵי אַבָּא בַּר אַחָא כַּרְסַלָּא מִכַּפְרִי הֲווֹ?
phrases.english: were all children of Abba bar Acha Karsala from Kafri?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכִי הֲוָה מַעֲשֶׂה, וְהָאָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sharpens the question of step 19 by ruling out the simple answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The simple answer that רב was only a sister's son
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known teaching makes רב's father a brother of רבי חייא. So רב was a brother's son, just like רבה בר חנה, and the different title is still unexplained.

steps.title: רב was related through both parents
steps.stepSummary: רב was a brother's son who was also a sister's son. רבה בר חנה was only a brother's son.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב was a brother's son who was also a sister's son. רבה בר חנה was a brother's son who was not a sister's son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב was related to רבי חייא on both sides of his family. רבי חייא used the title that showed this extra connection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both nephews were brothers' sons, so the teaching from step 20 is correct. But רב was also a sister's son, and רבה בר חנה was not. Calling רב 'my sister's son' points to the extra family tie he had.
steps.whatToRemember: Both רב and רבה בר חנה were sons of רבי חייא's brothers. רב was also a sister's son, which is why רבי חייא called him 'my sister's son.'

phrases.aramaic: רַב בַּר אֲחוּהּ דַּהֲוָה בַּר אֲחָתֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Rav was his brother's son who was also his sister's son,

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר חָנָה בַּר אֲחוּהּ דְּלָאו בַּר אֲחָתֵיהּ.
phrases.english: Rabba bar Chana was his brother's son who was not his sister's son.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב בַּר אֲחוּהּ דַּהֲוָה בַּר אֲחָתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20 and the question of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both facts are true: the family relationship was double
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רב's father was רבי חייא's brother, רב should have been called 'my brother's son.'
steps.terutzMaskana: רב was both a brother's son and a sister's son. The title 'my sister's son' points to the extra relationship that רבה בר חנה did not have.

steps.title: Introducing a second answer about the title 'sister's son'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא signals that it will offer another explanation for why רבי חייא called רב 'my sister's son.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, you can say a different answer:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It is about to give a second reason why רבי חייא called רב 'my sister's son.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer, that רב was both a brother's son and a sister's son, still stands. This phrase does not reject it. It just opens a second, separate way to solve the same question, and that second answer comes at the start of the next עמוד.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you want, say': the formula the גמרא uses to bring a second, alternative answer

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as the גמרא rejecting the first answer. 'אי בעית אימא' means both answers can work, and the גמרא is just giving you another option.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a second answer to the question in step 19, next to the answer already given in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative explanation (announced here; its content comes in the next line)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only way to explain 'my sister's son' is the double family connection given in step 21.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is another possible explanation as well, which the גמרא is about to present.
